findings.title: Round 1's F03 is reopened: the added safe-write instruction claims to use the triage agent's adaptation but inlines $(cat file) into a Python triple-quoted string literal inside python -c source code, so file content containing its own """ sequence breaks out of the string and causes a SyntaxError.
findings.evidence: .claude/agents/idea-planner.md:119-141 and agent-workflows/idea-planner-agent.md; contrast agent-workflows/idea-triage-agent.md:106-112, which substitutes $(cat file) into a quoted CLI argument (--text "$(cat ...)"). Reproduced with a draft.md containing a fenced code block with """A triple-quoted docstring...""": `uv run python -c "... check_plan_conformance(\"\"\"$(cat draft.md)\"\"\", depends_on=[], documents={}) ..."` → SyntaxError: invalid syntax.
findings.consequence: The patch adopts the $(cat) syntax but not the safety property, and introduces a new failure mode narrower than the one it closes.
findings.condition: Round-1 owner ruling: fix (adopt idea-triage's write-to-file-then-$(cat) rule).
findings.minimal_fix: Pass the file path to a small Python script/stdin (python -c "... = open(sys.argv[1]).read() ..." path) or read via stdin; never interpolate file bytes into Python source text.
